title: H100 benchmark results (Jan 2026) — profile pack v1 matrix
content:
Context / what this is
- This sheet captures Jan 2026 H100 benchmark runs used to validate the initial tuning profiles pack defaults before runtime-1.22.
- Runs are intended to be reproducible via benchmark-lab (see linked PR). Raw logs are in benchmark-lab artifacts; this doc is the summarized “what we believe + known weirdness”.
- Key comparisons:
  (A) baseline runtime-1.21 defaults (no profile pack)
  (B) profile pack enabled w/ H100 default profile (profile_id=h100-sxm-prod-default)
  (C) kernel variant change for attention (v3 vs v2 fallback) and scheduler bucket changes

Environment (most runs unless specified)
- GPU: NVIDIA H100 SXM (80GB)
- Node: 8x H100 SXM, NVLink (HGX)
- Driver: 550.54.14
- CUDA: 12.4
- Runtime build: runtime-main @ 1b7f4d2 (varies per section; see each run row)
- TensorRT-LLM: n/a (Redwood runtime kernels)
- MIG: disabled
- Power: default; no manual cap
- Cluster region: us-east-1 (benchmark-lab)

Model set / workload buckets
- M1: Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (BF16)
- M2: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (BF16)
- M3: Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct (BF16)
- M4: Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct (BF16)
- Buckets (prompt_tokens / output_tokens / concurrency):
  S1 “chat-short”: 128 / 128 / c=16
  S2 “chat-medium”: 512 / 256 / c=16
  L1 “long-prefill”: 4096 / 128 / c=8
  L2 “long-long”: 8192 / 256 / c=4
  D1 “decode-heavy”: 256 / 1024 / c=8
- Metrics reported:
  - E2E latency (ms) for request: p50 / p95 / p99
  - Throughput: output tokens/sec per GPU (tok/s/GPU) and cluster aggregate when available
  - GPU util (%): mean during steady state
  - HBM used (GB): peak observed on GPU0 (approx; taken from nvidia-smi sampler)
  - Scheduler queue time (ms): p95 (when instrumentation available)


Summary (high level)
- H100 default profile improves throughput in most buckets (+6% to +14% tok/s/GPU) without material p95 regressions when scheduler buckets are enabled.
- Biggest wins are from attention kernel v3 on long-prefill buckets (L1/L2) and from better decode batching in D1.
- One regression was observed on mixed-length traffic simulations (not in the simple buckets) tied to an overly aggressive batching default; reverted in pr-24988. See “Anomalies / reruns”.

Table 2 — Attention kernel v2 vs v3 (H100) — Long context focus
- Goal: validate pr-24911 kernel variant v3 improves long-prefill without new fallback cliffs.
- Same profile settings otherwise. Kernel choice exported in runtime metrics (kernel_choice=attn_v3 or attn_fallback).

Columns: run_id | date | git_sha | kernel | bucket | p50_ms | p95_ms | p99_ms | tok/s/GPU | gpu_util_% | kernel_fallback_rate_% | notes

h100-0118-kv2 | 2026-01-18 | c03d11b | attn_v2 | L1 | 954 | 1402 | 1738 | 103 | 79 | 0.2 | baseline for kernel comp
h100-0118-kv3 | 2026-01-18 | e92a7a4 | attn_v3 | L1 | 918 | 1355 | 1676 | 110 | 80 | 0.4 | +6.8% tok/s/GPU; p95 -3.4%

h100-0118-kv2b | 2026-01-18 | c03d11b | attn_v2 | L2 | 1748 | 2588 | 3240 | 88 | 81 | 0.3 | L2 is noisier; watch p99
h100-0118-kv3b | 2026-01-18 | e92a7a4 | attn_v3 | L2 | 1690 | 2508 | 3142 | 94 | 82 | 0.6 | +6.8% tok/s/GPU; p99 -3.0%

Notes:
- Fallback rate increased slightly but remains <1%. When it spikes >5% we typically saw driver mismatch or shape edge cases (see anomalies).
- Isabella’s microbench indicates v3 is more sensitive to very large batch*seq for prefill; current guard should avoid worst cases.


Table 3 — Scheduler buckets (mixed prefill/decode) — Effect on tail latency
- Compares scheduler changes from pr-24895 (workload buckets, queue policy).
- Workload: synthetic mixed distribution (60% S1, 25% S2, 10% L1, 5% D1), concurrency target 32 total.

Columns: run_id | date | git_sha | scheduler_mode | p50_ms | p95_ms | p99_ms | tok/s/GPU | scheduler_queue_p95_ms | notes

h100-0120-s0 | 2026-01-20 | 7ac19f0 | legacy | 260 | 820 | 1475 | 136 | 210 | legacy shows long tail under mixed prompts
h100-0120-s1 | 2026-01-20 | 4dff210 | bucketed_v1 | 255 | 690 | 1088 | 134 | 95 | tail improved; small throughput drop (expected)
h100-0122-s2 | 2026-01-22 | 1b7f4d2 | bucketed_v1+tuned_limits | 258 | 705 | 1125 | 138 | 102 | recovered throughput w/ tuned queue limits

Interpretation:
- Bucketed scheduling is clearly beneficial for p99 under mixed lengths, even when throughput is held roughly constant.
- Recommendation: keep bucketed scheduling enabled in H100 default profile; expose queue limit knobs and ensure queue_p95 is on dashboards.


Table 4 — Memory / KV cache changes (compaction thresholds) — Stability checks
- Related to pr-24902. Tests focused on long-long (L2) and decode-heavy (D1) where KV pressure is highest.

Columns: run_id | date | git_sha | kv_compaction | bucket | p99_ms | tok/s/GPU | hbm_peak_GB | compaction_time_ms_per_req_p95 | oom_count | notes

h100-0123-m0 | 2026-01-23 | 9b03a8e | baseline | L2 | 3198 | 90 | 75.6 | 0.0 | 0 | no compaction instrumentation
h100-0123-m1 | 2026-01-23 | 6e7c2fd | tuned_v1 | L2 | 3140 | 92 | 74.8 | 8.5 | 0 | slightly lower peak HBM; small compaction overhead
h100-0123-m2 | 2026-01-23 | 6e7c2fd | tuned_v1 | D1 | 2268 | 120 | 67.2 | 3.1 | 0 | stable

Notes:
- No OOMs observed on H100 SXM 80GB with these settings in this limited matrix.
- We still need a longer “soak” run with bursty concurrency ramps to confirm fragmentation estimates are predictive; Omar to follow up with more counters in runtime.


Anomalies / reruns / things we don’t trust yet
1) 2026-01-24: p99 regression in mixed workload simulation
- Symptom: mixed workload p99 moved from ~1.1s to ~1.35s on H100 for a canary-like traffic mix.
- Suspected cause: batching default too aggressive in one bucket (decode-heavy) causing queue buildup.
- Action: revert default in pr-24988; rerun mixed test.
- Rerun result (post-revert):
  - run_id h100-0126-r1 | 2026-01-26 | git_sha 2d9ce10 | bucketed_v1+tuned_limits+revert_batch | p99_ms=1138 | tok/s/GPU=137 | queue_p95_ms=104
- Conclusion: keep revert; adjust acceptance thresholds to catch p99 deltas >10% in perf-canary.

2) 2026-01-17: kernel fallback spikes on one node
- Symptom: kernel_fallback_rate 12–18% with attn_v3 on L2; tok/s/GPU dropped ~9%.
- Root cause: node had driver 545.xx (out of baseline); not caught by harness at the time.
- Fix: benchmark-lab runner now records driver and hard-fails when out of allowed set (change in benchmark-lab pr-913 follow-up, pending merge).
- Note to self: ensure profile compatibility checks in runtime match what benchmark-lab enforces.

3) Noise due to background GPU clocks / thermal
- We saw occasional ~3–5% variance in tok/s/GPU across back-to-back runs even with same git/profile.
- Hypothesis: node sharing / power management; mitigations:
  - add warmup period (2 min) before recording steady state
  - record GPU clocks and power draw in artifacts


Acceptance threshold suggestions (draft; for SRE gate discussion)
- For H100 default profile change (same model + bucket), block rollout if:
  - p95 increases >5% AND p99 increases >10% on any of S1/S2/L1/D1 (single run)
  - OR tok/s/GPU decreases >5% on any two buckets
  - OR kernel_fallback_rate >5% sustained for >10 minutes in L1/L2
- Warn-only if p50 increases but p95/p99 stable (usually indicates scheduling tuning, not a tail issue).


Next actions
- Marcus: add a “mixed traffic” workload to the standard benchmark matrix (not just pure buckets).
- Isabella/Grace: validate attn_v3 guard rails on extreme shapes (16k prefill) on H100; decide whether to keep fallback or reduce coverage.
- Omar: ensure fragmentation + compaction counters are tagged by profile_id/profile_version and present in the Runtime Profiles dashboard.
- Rina: refresh this sheet with Feb reruns after pr-25063 trace instrumentation lands (separate queue vs compute time).
